newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux says sells Husqvarna unit.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux says sells Husqvarna unit.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB said on Thursday that it was selling Husqvarna sewing machines to investment fund company Industri Kapital.
The sale would give Electrolux a capital gain of about 600 million crowns ($81.2 million), the company said in a statement. ($ = 7.392 Swedish Crowns)
"Electrolux has signed a preliminary agreement with the investment fund Industri Kapital for divestment of the group's operation in the sewing machines product area," Electrolux said.
Husqvarna sales in 1996 totalled 850 million crowns. The unit has around 700 employees.
"The divestment is scheduled for completion on March 31, 1997 and will generate a capital gain of approximately 600 million crowns for Electrolux," it said.
Electrolux president and CEO Leif Johansson said the move was in line with the group's strategy to concentrate its activities.

"The divestment is in line with our programme for streamlining the group's structure and releasing resources for expansion within our core areas. Industri Kapital will be an active owner for Husqvarna Sewing Machines," he said.
Electrolux said Industri Kapital was a leading investment fund in northern Europe, managing capital totalling more than three billion crowns.
"Industri Kapital is looking forward to participating in the international development of Husqvarna Sewing Machines," said Bjorn Saven, president of Industri Kapital, in the statement.
